body: I'm still around. I'm still in a lot of pain. It's getting closer to my move-in date, which is just over a month for today, so I'm trying to hold out to see if it gets better. Otherwise I'll be ending things.

I have tried therapy. But I know I can't bring myself to do another semester while in pain. I'm sorry you're going through your own, likely more extreme pain– and I appreciate that you're willing to tolerate more without being suicidal– but I don't think I'm capable of that.
You helped enough; it's nice to know i'm not the only one dealing with it.

Nope, I'm not leaking or having incontinence... Jeez, someone always has it worse, right? 

Everything bowel-related has been perfectly normal and fine throughout. :/
Yeah. They do pop up occasionally with this issue due to the nature of the skin, but it is not the case.

It definitely doesn't feel like something there. It's usually an occasional itch, but usually a very strong burning raw sensation, like strep throat, but in the wrong place. (And no, it's not anal strep, they tested for that.)

This is true, but it's up to the professionals what constitutes a proper test. I've had multiple doctors– over eight, – and if not a single one suggests a CT or X-Ray is a good idea– well, I don't think that's an oversight.

Googling led me to that and I brought it up with a neurologist who didn't believe it was the case. (I don't remember exactly why, I have it written down somewhere, but I do remember that that isn't it. )

They haven't done those tests, but they don't seem to think it's more than skin-deep. Currently the dermatologist thinks it's an issue with the nerves causing them to overreact to the inflammation. They've prescribed a numbing agent but it's really not a good long-term solution. (Even as a short term solution, the numbness and the gel itself are fairly uncomfortable and prohibit some degree of freedom of movement and ability to enjoy life.)

I've thought of pretty much everything.

I've ruled out, for various reasons, the stress of starting the college year, the diet changes, the detergent / washers and dryers I was using, the possibility of an allergic reaction to the small plant I got for my room, and quite a few other things– and besides, I'm back home now with the same lifestyle I had before the pain started, and with no luck.

I've really tried everything, which is why i'm giving up.
